title: Alter and Coleman: contingent grounding does not make consciousness inefficacious

statements.text: Russellian monism is consistent with the metaphysical contingency of quiddistic grounding, and that contingency does not imply that consciousness lacks physical efficacy, since causation in general is metaphysically contingent. Nomological contingency would imply it, but the laws of quiddistic grounding are among the laws of nature and rule swapped quiddities out. A necessitarian version also stays open.

sources.quote: But such a metaphysical contingency thesis does not entail that consciousness lacks physical efficacy.
In short, causation is arguably metaphysically contingent.
Contra Howell, necessitarianism is a viable option for Russellian monists.
